description: Fig. 8 is a three-panel composite of line-with-marker charts comparing three optimization algorithms for an Extra Trees yield-strength model. All panels share the same x-axis categories — Grid Search-ET, Bayesian-ET and Our — under the axis title "Comparison of optimization algorithms", and a smooth black curve is drawn through the three data points; every panel has a light-to-dark purple/grey gradient background and a black frame. (a) plots RMSE on a y-axis spanning 30-90 with ticks every 10 and prints 80.239 (Grid Search-ET), 80.721 (Bayesian-ET) and 31.6 (Our); the fitted curve peaks above 80 between the first two points, then falls steeply, and the "Our" point is enclosed in a red dashed circle. (b) plots MAPE on a y-axis from 4 to 13 and prints 11.037, 11.423 and 4.39, with the "Our" point again circled in red. (c) plots R² on a y-axis from 0.970 to 1.000 in 0.005 steps and prints 0.972, 0.976 and 0.997, the last circled. Together the three panels make one argument: the model denoted "Our" is lowest in error and highest in R².

observations.observation: Panel (a) plots RMSE with printed data labels 80.239 (Grid Search-ET), 80.721 (Bayesian-ET) and 31.6 (Our) on a y-axis spanning 30 to 90 with ticks every 10 units.
In panel (a) the 'Our' data point is highlighted with a red dashed circle, marking the lowest RMSE of the three algorithms.
Panel (b) plots MAPE with printed data labels 11.037 (Grid Search-ET), 11.423 (Bayesian-ET) and 4.39 (Our); the y-axis spans 4 to 13 with integer ticks and the 'Our' point is circled in red.
Panel (c) plots R² with printed data labels 0.972 (Grid Search-ET), 0.976 (Bayesian-ET) and 0.997 (Our) on a y-axis from 0.970 to 1.000 with ticks every 0.005; the 0.997 point is circled in red.
The third x-axis category in all three panels is labelled 'Our' rather than with an algorithm name, so the algorithm identity is not stated in the figure itself.
In panels (a) and (b) the smoothed curve bulges to a maximum between the Grid Search-ET and Bayesian-ET points; that interior extremum carries no printed value.
All three panels have a vertical purple-to-grey gradient background, black axis frames, and the shared x-axis title 'Comparison of optimization algorithms'.
The extra-trees model optimized by grid search and Bayesian optimization gave RMSE values of 80.239 MPa and 80.721 MPa, whereas the GA-Extra trees model gave 31.60 MPa.
The citing text states that the GA-Extra trees model also showed superior MAPE and R², so optimizing the Extra Trees model with GA is the most suitable approach.
The study compares GA with alternative optimization technologies such as Bayesian optimization using the same model performance evaluation index.
The caption describes the figure only as a 'Performance comparison of different optimization algorithms', which identifies the three metrics only via the panel axis labels.
The figure identifies 'Our' with the GA-Extra trees configuration only indirectly: the printed axis label is 'Our', while the citing sentences assign the GA-Extra trees identity to it.

subfigures.description: Line-plus-marker plot of RMSE (y-axis 30-90, ticks every 10) versus optimization algorithm (Grid Search-ET, Bayesian-ET, Our). Data labels printed: 80.239, 80.721 and 31.6. The smooth curve rises to an unlabelled peak between the first two points and drops steeply to the third, which is highlighted with a red dashed circle.

Line-plus-marker plot of MAPE (y-axis 4-13, integer ticks) versus the same three algorithms. Data labels printed: 11.037, 11.423 and 4.39; the 4.39 point for 'Our' is circled in red. The interpolating curve again overshoots between the first two points and falls steeply afterwards.

Line-plus-marker plot of R² (y-axis 0.970 to 1.000, ticks every 0.005) versus the same three algorithms. Data labels printed: 0.972, 0.976 and 0.997; the 0.997 value for 'Our' is circled in red. Here the curve rises monotonically, gently at first and steeply toward 'Our'.
